title: Truth from the earth (Genesis Rabbah 8:5)
hookLine: kindness and truth argue over making humans; God casts truth to the ground, and it springs up (Psalm 85:12)
tomorrow: if God called it all very good, what about our worst urges?

cards: A group chat, one question: should we invite him? One friend says yes, he's generous. Another says no, he lies.
A third says yes, he does the right thing when it counts. A fourth says no, he starts fights. Genesis Rabbah puts that same split vote in heaven, just before the first human being is made.
And the voters are four virtues.

teach.b: Rabbi Simon tells it, from a psalm: "Mercy and truth are met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other." Kindness says: create him, he'll do acts of kindness. Truth says: don't, he's all lies.
Righteousness says: create him, he'll do righteous deeds. Peace says: don't, he's all quarreling. Let both sides make their best case.

teach.h: WHAT PEOPLE CAN DO, OR DO.
teach.b: Kindness and righteousness see what people can do: the meal carried to a grieving house, the honest judge. Truth and peace see what people actually do: the lie that slides out, the fight nobody needed.
Truth isn't being cruel. Truth is being accurate. Then God does something startling.
He takes truth and casts it to the ground. The angels protest: would You shame Your own seal? Let truth rise up from the earth.
And the midrash lands on the psalm's next verse: "Truth springeth out of the earth." So who won? Read one way, kindness did: people got made over an honest objection.
Read another way, truth wasn't defeated, only planted. It went into the ground people walk on, and grows back up from there, through them.
On that reading, the creature made in spite of truth is also where truth comes back.

how: Psalm 85 is read in some Jewish prayer books among the psalms for particular days, and Genesis Rabbah 8:5 is a favorite text in study circles on honesty and kindness.

games.q: what does “truth from the earth” mean?
o: truth thrown down that grows back through people
an honest farmer whose harvest feeds his town
the clay God used to shape the first person

games.q: the four votes — tap the pairs.

s: in this midrash, truth loses and is gone for good
it's cast to the ground, and the psalm says it springs back up.
the angels call truth God's own seal
they protest: would You shame Your seal?
all four virtues agreed people should be made

games.q: a classmate says: if truth said people are liars, God just ignored the facts. what's the best case for both sides of this midrash?
o: truth was accurate; God didn't erase it but planted it, and it grows back.
truth was being mean, so God threw it out for good.
truth won; people weren't made until they stopped lying.
games.why: truth's objection was honest. God cast it down, and the psalm the angels quote says it springs out of the earth.

practice: Find one true thing you've been sitting on, small enough to say: I was wrong about that, or I miss them, or I need help with this. Say it out loud once, quietly, even if only to the room.
Then let it rest in the quiet, like a seed that's just gone into the ground.

orig.note: Hebrew: truth, the virtue God casts to the ground in Genesis Rabbah 8:5.
